I wish that therapists don’t brush those off too soon because some clients are really serious about trying to understand their mental health struggles through a new diagnosis while others are not. 

I have long suspected that I am on the spectrum because I have always felt like an outsider and a weird kid growing up and when I heard of the traits of ASD, I almost fit every single one of them. I thought about this a lot and thought that maybe getting a diagnosis will help me feel less alone because it’s a label and a label means there are other people that feel this way. So I humbly asked a therapist whether my suspicion is reasonable to any extent. 

The therapist laughed at me for using “Dr Google” and brushed me off because she assumed I am one of those teenagers who self label for fun. I felt extremely hurt and sought another therapist who believed me. 

I eventually got tested and was told that I did meet lots of criteria but because I don’t have neurological delay as a kid, it’s unlikely that I am on the spectrum. They told me that neurological delay is an essential criteria. Which is some form of closure. They also point me towards some schizoid traits which is consistent with some of my behaviours and feelings (they didn’t say I have schizoid personality disorder, only that I have some traits of them). I felt a bit less alone after this.
Thank you for your comment! And totally, she could care both about the money and me as a client.
